notes: Product/market: VS Code extension with inline autocompletions + larger multi-line streaming completions.
Primary pain: unpredictable tail latency on longer inline completions; poor perceived IDE UX when suggestions stall.
Quote from CTO: 'We need sub-60ms inline suggestions 95% of the time — anything slower is disruptive.'
POC goals: achieve median inference latency <40ms for single-line completions and <120ms 95th for 256-token streaming bursts.
Architectural ask: pin model by workspace/project; allow canary version rollouts; opt-in quantized variant for low-cost users.
Auth/tenant: must support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning; want audit logs per-user for compliance reviews.
Rate limits: need per-user and per-organization throttles; free tier devs get lower QPS, paid orgs require burst windows.
Billing: prefer usage-based hosted API for now; evaluating Dedicated for predictable latency during peak dev hours.
Security: ask for KMS integration for key wrapping and 12-month log retention with easy export for audits.
Integrations: VS Code extension will call Redwood streaming endpoints directly from client background process — concern about client secrets and token rotation.
Workarounds discussed: short-lived tokens via Redwood auth proxy; embed rate-limiter at extension server side.
Internal stakeholders: CTO (decision), Head of Product (UX), Infra lead (integration), Security (SAML/KMS signoff).
Open items: demo attach with exact token/connection flow; latency dashboard with traces for suggestion latency per-filetype.
AE notes: keep pricing tier options simple — show Hosted API + burst Dedicated as two scenarios.
requirements_summary: VS Code-centric integration: streaming completion API with robust reconnection + incremental tokens
Inline suggestion latency SLO: median <40ms, 95th <60ms for single-line completions
Long-form streaming: maintain steady throughput for 256-token + support cancellation from editor
Model/version controls: workspace pinning + automated canary rollout policy
Auth & provisioning: SAML SSO, SCIM, short-lived tokens for extension clients
Observability: per-route latency, user-level cost breakdown, and logs exported to customer SIEM
Rate limits: per-user and per-org quotas with burst windows and graceful error payloads for the client
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (hosted POC): integrate extension with hosted streaming API, collect traces, measure latency
Phase 2 (security review): SAML/SCIM testbed + KMS keywrap validation
Phase 3 (scale test): simulate 200 concurrent devs, measure 95th percentile streaming latency
Phase 4 (go-live): choose Hosted vs Dedicated based on latency and cost analysis; finalize contract
